canonical_statement: In the regular integral highest-weight setting for a complex semisimple Lie algebra, the Jordan-Holder multiplicities of simple highest-weight modules in Verma modules are the values at 1 of the corresponding Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials, with indices and normalization exactly as in Kazhdan-Lusztig (1979), Conjecture 1.5.
domain_and_universes: Planned: a complex semisimple Lie algebra (or source-equivalent root datum), its Weyl group, a regular integral block of BGG category O, and finite Jordan-Holder multiplicities; exact Lean universes and structures remain open.
quantifiers: semisimple Lie-theoretic datum satisfying the hypotheses of the source statement
Weyl-group indices in the source-specified Bruhat-order relation
hypotheses: index/order and normalization conditions from the pinned source statement
conclusion: The relevant Verma-module composition multiplicity equals the source-corresponding Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial evaluated at 1.
excluded_degenerate_cases: Singular and parabolic category O, affine Kac-Moody variants, arbitrary Coxeter systems without the representation-theoretic datum, coefficient positivity alone, and the definition/existence of the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis are not the canonical root.
